data.why: The research site's charts read committed, pre-exported JSON in web/public/data/ (produced from results/example/ by scripts/export_site_data.py); nothing needs to be uploaded or synthesized.

goals: Compare latency, throughput, deadline compliance and fairness across the four scheduling policies (fifo, priority, edf, wfq) under the four workload types
Check whether a policy's median-latency win comes at the cost of tail latency or starvation (p50 vs p99, max wait)
Verify a chart's claimed number by following its linked source CSV, SHA-256 digest and the exact command that produced it
Assess per-tenant fairness (Jain's index) under tenant skew and relate it to the tenant latency skew chart
Read the failover and fencing experiments to see the measured cost of a crash, freeze and partition on dispatch
Look for pending/not-yet-publishable experiments and read the corrections the export pipeline forced in the report

review.summary: This tree reflects the research site faithfully: its goal and phases match the README's research question (policy effects on latency, throughput, deadlines, fairness and starvation) and the site's provenance-first purpose, and every screen I sampled supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: the orientation phase promises Architecture and Method but covers only the Overview, deadline compliance has no task of its own, and the Overview's findings-to-evidence links are not captured as a feature.
